page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 for vector operations, AES cryptography acceleration, and SHA extensions. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Additionally, the instance includes 2458 GB of bundled local storage, though it does not feature any dedicated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core computational capabilities and memory throughput. The server achieves strong performance in multi-threaded tasks, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU score of 61043.75 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 62149.0. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient for large block operations, reaching 291.88 GB/sec for read-only and 134.9 GB/sec for write operations. Single-core performance remains in the average tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1649.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1899.49. Cryptographic and vector execution capabilities are highly pronounced, with strong results in Passmark extended instructions and encryption tests.

With its balanced resource allocation and high-capacity local storage, the D64d_v5 offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high resource density without the premium of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated tiers. The strong multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and database operation benchmarks make this instance highly suitable for relational databases, static web serving, software build pipelines, and parallel data processing. However, the average single-core performance and lack of hardware accelerators make it less optimal for single-threaded applications or heavy deep learning training workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D64d_v5 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM. It features 2458 GB of bundled local storage and operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Benchmarks reveal strong multi-core performance, with a Passmark CPU score of 61043.75, and strong memory bandwidth for large block operations. Single-core performance and LLM inference speeds fall into the average tier. The instance is highly efficient for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, and database operations due to its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high-capacity local storage. It is well-suited for relational databases, static web serving, and parallel data processing, though it lacks GPU acceleration for intensive machine learning tasks.
